For a person entering college with arms that haven't been worked out in years, what is a good weekly routine to increase muscle mass? (specifically biceps and abdominal muscles)

I was looking at this, and was wondering if any of you had any critiques. The guide only recommends one session per week, is that really all I need to start? It also says I have to keep that workout up for 3-4 months before I should go intermediate.

Anyway if you have any tips that would be great, thanks.

Check out both the Scott Herman and Athlean-X YouTube pages. They have a lot of good workouts up there, plenty to base an entire routine off of.

Edit: Just skimming through the page you linked to, there seems to be a lot of good workouts in there. They say to train "once per week", but that's with the assumption that you're working out the rest of your body on those other days. Don't forget that the biceps work as a stabilizer/assistant muscle with a lot of other workouts too (so when you're training back, you'll still also be hitting your biceps a bit).

If you're looking for mass my best advice would be to develop a FULL workout routine and stick to it, going to the gym 3-5 days a week.

I do arms once a week, though some of my chest days and shoulder/back days do involve some tricep and bicep usage as well. You generally want to do a good workout every 5-7 days to avoid over-training.

I do roughly 8-10 exercises for arms with 3 sets of 12-10-8 and increasing weight. Some core ones you should always be doing are:

  • Bicep Curl
  • Hammer Curls
  • Dips

These three exercises work out all three major muscle groups in your arm that makes your arms look bigger. You can add a forearm exercise as well.

Came here to say the same thing as /u/chance, both guys have great info on building muscle the right way. I prefer Athlean X but Scott has great advice and I just used bits from both. I will say this, work both biceps and triceps on the same day. I do a four exercise routine for my arms two for bicep and two for tricep and I alternate. Incline barbell curls, cable tricep pull downs, hammer curls, dumbell skull crushers. I find that 5 sets of each at 8 reps at around 80% of my max weight is a great workout and only takes about 20 minutes. The stronger you get you can start extending that or upping the weights. Things I have learned from both channels. 2 days rest for arms is important, also form is key over weight lifted, go as heavy as you can but you have to keep good form. Nutrition, nutrition, nutrition, make sure you eat enough but also the right kind of calories or you wont build muscle. Some people respond to more reps less weight some to heavy weights and less reps. You will figure it out as you go and just use the one that works. Also be prepared to change up your workout every 6 weeks or so, don't just keep doing the same thing over and over, change helps stimulate muscle growth.
